Investment rationale: hard sign flips amplify noise whenever range momentum is near zero and effectively add a fitted threshold; scaling body-efficiency acceleration by proportional range expansion preserves the breakout-regime interaction with fewer implicit degrees of freedom and smoother cross-sectional ranks.

Collapse the nested Ma-then-Diff structure into an explicit short-vs-long body-efficiency spread: (Ma((close-open)/(high-low),10) - Ma((close-open)/(high-low),40)) / Ma(high-low,20), dropping the separate range-momentum multiplier. Stabilize the intraday body ratio before any smoothing by flooring the denominator: Ma((close-open)/Max(high-low, Ma(high-low,20)), 20) in place of Ma((close-open)/(high-low), 20). Investment rationale: dividing by raw high-low overweights tiny-range bars whose body ratios are numerically unstable and often sample-specific; anchoring the range floor to typical daily range removes sensitivity to microstructure spikes without adding a separate interaction or variance normalization layer.
